annotations.description: Choosing to be on the draw is almost always wrong in competitive Magic, especially with a hand full of discard spells (Thoughtseize, Inquisition of Kozilek). Being on the play lets you strip key cards from the opponent's hand before they can use them on turn 1, which is the entire point of running these spells. The reasoning given ('being on the draw gives us an extra card') is a common misconception — in Modern, tempo and the ability to interact before the opponent's first meaningful turn is far more valuable than the extra card, particularly with proactive disruption like hand attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to let Gem25F Libby go first (being on the draw)
annotations.betterLine: Choose to go first (Sonnet Coach). Playing turn 1 Thoughtseize or Inquisition of Kozilek on the play strips the opponent's best card before they can deploy anything, giving a massive tempo advantage.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Marsh Flats is slightly suboptimal. With Thoughtseize and Inquisition of Kozilek both in hand (wanting to cast a discard spell this turn), any of the black sources work. However, Marsh Flats is generally better to play first because: (1) it thins the deck, (2) it can fetch Swamp anyway, and (3) you have Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth which will make all lands Swamps later, making Marsh Flats unable to tap for colored mana without fetching. Additionally, against an artifact deck (Mox Opal, Mishra's Bauble suggest Emry/artifact strategies), cracking Marsh Flats now preserves the option to play Ifnir Deadlands or Urborg later when they're more relevant. The Swamp in hand becomes a worse draw-equivalent later compared to having already thinned with Marsh Flats.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Swamp as their land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Marsh Flats, crack it to fetch a Swamp (paying 1 life), then cast Thoughtseize or Inquisition of Kozilek. This thins the deck and preserves future land drop flexibility.

annotations.description: Against an artifact-based deck (Mox Opal, Mishra's Bauble visible), Inquisition of Kozilek likely hits most relevant cards since artifact strategies tend to be low-curve. The opponent's deck appears to run cards like Emry (CMC 3), Welding Jar (CMC 0), Weapons Manufacturing (CMC 2), and other cheap artifacts - almost all hittable by Inquisition. Paying 2 life with Thoughtseize is unnecessary when Inquisition would likely see and hit the same targets. The 2 life matters against aggressive artifact strategies that can deal incidental damage.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Inquisition of Kozilek to save 2 life, as most cards in the opponent's artifact-heavy deck are likely CMC 3 or less. Save Thoughtseize for later when you might need to hit a higher-CMC card, or when you have better information about what they're holding.

annotations.description: The opponent cast Thoughtseize targeting Gem25F Libby, and Libby is being asked to select a target for Mishra's Bauble's activated ability (which is a separate item on the stack). However, looking more carefully at the decision, Libby is choosing who to target with Mishra's Bauble - themselves or the opponent. Targeting yourself with Mishra's Bauble when you could instead look at the top card of your opponent's library is a significant missed opportunity. Knowing what your opponent will draw next turn provides much more strategic value than knowing your own top card, especially early in the game when you have no scry or library manipulation to take advantage of that information. The reasoning given ('to better organize my own library') doesn't even make sense since Mishra's Bauble doesn't reorganize your library - it only lets you look at the top card.

Weapons Manufacturing is strong but requires other artifacts to enter to generate value. Taking Emry shuts down their recursion engine and leaves them with enchantments that need artifacts to trigger, while the player has Inquisition of Kozilek in hand to potentially take another piece next turn.

annotations.description: Playing a second Mox Opal while the first is on the battlefield violates the Legend Rule - one must be sacrificed immediately. The player has only 1 artifact on the battlefield (the first Mox Opal), so even after the second enters and one is sacrificed, they'll still have just 1 artifact, far from the 3 needed for Metalcraft. This wastes a Mox Opal for no mana benefit. The correct sequence would be to play Welding Jar first (free artifact, getting to 2 artifacts), then play the land (Fiery Islet), then cast Emry (who costs {U} with 2 artifacts via Affinity), which mills 4 cards and adds another artifact creature. After Emry, Metalcraft would be active with 3+ artifacts, making the single Mox Opal functional.

annotations.description: Casting Nethergoyf before Inquisition of Kozilek is suboptimal sequencing. Inquisition of Kozilek should be cast first because: (1) It reveals the opponent's hand, giving crucial information about what threats/answers they have (like Emry, Engineered Explosives, etc.), which could inform whether to deploy Nethergoyf now or hold it. (2) After Inquisition resolves, there will be a sorcery (Inquisition) in the graveyard alongside the existing sorcery (Thoughtseize), but more importantly the opponent's discarded card could matter for planning. (3) Nethergoyf currently has power equal to the number of card types in the graveyard - right now there's just Sorcery (Thoughtseize), so it's a 1/2. Casting Inquisition first doesn't change this since it's also a sorcery. However, the information from Inquisition could reveal whether it's even safe to deploy Nethergoyf (e.g., opponent might have Engineered Explosives which could answer it). Playing the discard spell first is a fundamental sequencing principle - gather information before committing threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nethergoyf before casting Inquisition of Kozilek
annotations.betterLine: Cast Inquisition of Kozilek first to see the opponent's hand and strip their best card, then decide whether to deploy Nethergoyf or hold it based on that information

annotations.description: Playing Claws of Gix before Emry is suboptimal sequencing. With Mox Opal, Welding Jar, and Claws of Gix, they have 3 artifacts for Metalcraft on Mox Opal, but Emry with Affinity for artifacts already costs only U with 3 artifacts (Mox Opal, Welding Jar, Claws of Gix). However, the better line is to cast Emry first: with 3 artifacts already (Mox Opal, Welding Jar, + Claws of Gix cast first), Emry costs U. But actually, without Claws of Gix, they have 2 artifacts (Mox Opal, Welding Jar), so Emry costs 1U. They can tap Fiery Islet for U and need 1 more generic - but Mox Opal doesn't have Metalcraft with only 2 artifacts. So casting Claws of Gix first enables Metalcraft on Mox Opal, then they can tap both Mox Opal and Fiery Islet to cast Emry for 1U (reduced to U by 3 artifacts = free with affinity... wait: Emry costs 2U, with 3 artifacts affinity reduces by 2, so it costs U). With Metalcraft active, Mox Opal taps for any color. So Claws first, then Emry for U off Fiery Islet works. But they could also cast Emry for U and then Claws of Gix after. Actually the key question is: they played Claws of Gix and then skipped their attack and apparently didn't cast Emry. With Claws on the field (3 artifacts), Mox Opal has Metalcraft, they can tap Fiery Islet for U to cast Emry (cost reduced from 2U to U). They should have followed up with Emry to mill four cards and start recurring artifacts. Not casting Emry this turn when they could is the real missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Claws of Gix and then passed without casting Emry, Lurker of the Loch
annotations.betterLine: Cast Claws of Gix to enable Metalcraft, then cast Emry for U (Affinity reduces 2U to U with 3 artifacts) using Fiery Islet, milling four cards and enabling artifact recursion

annotations.description: The player chose Thoughtseize over Inquisition of Kozilek when both were in hand. Inquisition of Kozilek hits everything CMC 3 or less without the 2 life cost. The 2 life matters especially with Ifnir Deadlands also costing life. However, Thoughtseize does guarantee hitting Kappa Cannoneer if it's in hand, which Inquisition cannot. annotations.description: Gem25F Libby passed their precombat main phase without casting anything despite having the mana and artifacts to cast Kappa Cannoneer. Alternatively, casting Weapons Manufacturing first (1R via Fiery Islet + Mox Opal) would set up powerful synergies with artifacts entering.
